problem: Zero-shot object navigation methods in multi-floor environments over-emphasize exploration and lack explicit state handling, so robots get stuck at narrow spots, wander endlessly, or fail to find stair entrances. Their exploration also does not adapt to coverage, semantic cues and structure, so MLLM use is either too sparse (ASCENT, ApexNav) or too heavy (CogNav).
motivation: Multi-floor scenes are common (about 65% of HM3D scenes and 73% of MP3D scenes), and cross-floor episodes are where prior zero-shot methods fail most (VLFM gets 0.4 SR inter-floor). Robustness to entrapment and missed stairs, plus a good exploration/exploitation balance under a 500-step budget, should therefore matter more than better maps alone.
key_idea: A state machine switches the agent among Exploration (fast optimization-based thinking plus door-triggered slow MLLM thinking), Recovery (for stuck or wandering) and Reminiscing (revisit keypoints to verify missed targets or find stairs) states.
insight: The ablations show that each state and each exploration component contributes. On HM3D, EXP alone gets 72.3 SR only with REC+REM (68.9 without), and dynamic α/β plus the MLLM gives the best result (72.3 vs 68.5 for fixed weights without the MLLM). The gains concentrate on inter-floor episodes (62.5 SR vs 33.3 for ASCENT), which suggests that explicit handling of stair search and stuck recovery matters more than better intra-floor exploration (75.8 vs 72.6). Triggering the MLLM at doorframes, rather than only when no nearby frontier exists, also avoids wasted exploration of dead-end rooms.
method: State machine: S_exp is the initial state and is active while frontiers remain; S_rec triggers when the last N_rec steps show displacement below D_rec metres and returns to S_exp afterwards; S_rem triggers when the current floor has no new frontiers.

Maps: a per-floor visibility occupancy map from depth BEV (intra-floor and stair frontiers, following ASCENT), a value map V(f)=α·S_sem+β·S_dist using BLIP-2 similarity to MLLM-generated context prompts, and a KeyPoint Map of room entrances and open-visibility frontiers, each with a stored RGB observation.

Fast-thinking: chooses frontiers by J(f)=α(k)V(f)+β(k)I(f|F), where I is the expected uncertainty reduction (Gaussian-kernel information density over the FOV coverage area plus overlap with other frontiers). α and β adapt via an Exploration Reward ER(k) combining unexplored-area ratio, frontier density and time decay.

Slow-thinking: a doorframe detector triggers the MLLM (GPT-4o), which reasons over a local room/object topology (RAM object tags, Places365 room types, the visibility map and the RGB image) about which frontier or region likely contains the target.

Dual recovery: for distant frontiers, A* on the visibility map with interval-sampled intermediate waypoints; for nearby frontiers, the MLLM issues fine-grained action commands from the RGB image and local map. A pretrained PointNav policy is the base controller.

Reminiscing: after a floor is exhausted, the MLLM (1) reviews keypoints to find overlooked target locations, verifies them with the stored RGB, then approaches; (2) otherwise picks the keypoint most likely to hold a staircase entrance, goes there with PointNav, and aligns with MLLM-guided fine actions.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) as MLLM; BLIP-2 for value map; RAM, Places365, Grounding-DINO, SAM; pretrained PointNav policy
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, LOOK_UP/DOWN, STOP (frontier goals executed via PointNav)

numbers_note: Success radius is stated as 0.1 m in the task definition (unusual; the standard is 0.1 m for ObjectNav in some setups). The paper says 'validation split' without naming val explicitly, so the split is recorded as val. Other own-variant numbers (Qwen2.5-VL 71.4/34.5, Gemini 70.8/33.8 on HM3D) appear only in the ablations.
results: AERR-Nav reaches 72.3 SR / 35.6 SPL on HM3D and 47.9 SR / 18.7 SPL on MP3D, beating the strongest baseline ASCENT (65.4/33.5 on HM3D, 44.5/15.5 on MP3D). The gain is largest in inter-floor episodes: 62.5 SR vs 33.3 for ASCENT.
limitations: Depends on GPT-4o for the slow-thinking, recovery and reminiscing stages, with cost and latency not reported; open MLLMs such as Qwen2.5-VL score slightly lower (71.4 SR).
Evaluated only in simulation on HM3D and MP3D with hand-tuned state-trigger thresholds; no real-robot experiments.
The state-switching and reward hyperparameters (N_rec, D_rec, σ, α_min, β_max) are heuristic and their sensitivity is not analyzed; the SPL gain on HM3D over ASCENT is modest (+2.1).
